Four-level configuration ordering — Order is base.conf, sorted base.d/*.conf, base.local, sorted base.d/*.local. Candidate local precedes directory conf and directory local is omitted.

Before/after include graph and paired locals — Recursive before/current/after include traversal resolves relative names and included .local partners, avoids seen recursion. Candidate loader does not traverse INCLUDES.

INI lexical and error semantics — Reference ConfigParser normalization, inline semicolon comments, multiline continuation and typed conversion determine effective values; candidate keeps key case, does not implement reference inline comments, warns and skips malformed lines, treats every non-true boolean as false.

Cross-section and previous-value interpolation — Resolve section/key, default/key, known/key, __name__, ordinary % interpolation and escaped percent in context; previous overridden values remain accessible. Candidate only local/DEFAULT expansion and literal preservation for unknown variables.

Per-value provenance and unresolved data retention — Migration needs raw and effective values, source location/layer, definition parameters, include/override chain and asset hashes; reference determines effective behavior, provenance is replacement migration requirement. Current merge overwrites values and stores source only in warnings.

Definition Init and invocation parameter merging — Filter/action [Init], invocation brackets, jail settings, conditional options and recursive tags combine into effective definitions. Candidate selects a built-in from raw filter name and reduces action prefix to backend.

Global service and logging configuration — Import socket,pidfile,loglevel,logtarget,syslogsocket and early/late option precedence, preserving operational meaning. Candidate global native fields do not import fail2ban global config.

Global database and thread settings — dbfile None/:memory:/path, dbpurgeage and dbmaxmatches determine persistence/retention; Thread stacksize needs explicit semantic mapping/profile applicability. Candidate binary state path has no lossless import mapping.
Global allowipv6 control — Global auto/yes/no controls IPv6 support detection and DNS expansion. Candidate supports IPv6 but lacks equivalent global setting.

Effective jail inheritance including enabled and filter — Reference DEFAULT options apply to each jail, including enabled/filter/logpath and skip controls; candidate reads local enabled/filter/logpath and defaults absent enabled to false, so [DEFAULT] enabled=true is not preserved.

Unknown/custom options retained as parameter namespace — Port,protocol,chain,banaction and arbitrary user variables feed interpolation/definitions; fixed native jail struct cannot represent them. Preserve unused raw data and resolve consumed options before claiming full migration.
Time unit constants and aliases — Reference year=365.25 days and month=year/12=30.4375 days; candidate year365/month30. Reference aliases include dd/ww/hou etc.

Compound, fractional, arithmetic and sentinel time inputs — Reference converts arithmetic unit expressions and numeric values, including signed/fractional forms; candidate single unsigned integer + suffix cannot preserve them. Implement a bounded arithmetic language; never evaluate imported general code during inspect.

Multi-path glob expansion and head/tail syntax — Reference expands each newline path glob and parses optional final head/tail token; candidate preserves raw path and watches it literally, initially seeks EOF.

No-log skip and auto journal fallback — Reference skip_if_nologs and systemd_if_nologs alter missing-file outcome; auto journal fallback depends journalmatch and availability. Candidate source auto is built-in-filter-specific and lacks skip settings.

Durable file positions and startup replay — Reference stores path/hash/position, resumes durable offset unless tail and auto-seeks relevant history. Candidate file offsets are memory-only and initially EOF.

Rotation and partial-line boundaries — Reference uses inode,size,first-line hash and complete encoded lines. Candidate implements inotify rotation/copytruncate and line buffering; equality under delayed writes/rename still requires paired fixtures.
General journal match algebra — Reference journalmatch supports field groups and plus disjunction, multiple added match lists, removal/reset. Candidate hardcodes sshd selectors.
Journal backend parameters and environment — journalpath,journalfiles,journalflags,namespace,rotated and F2B_SYSTEMD_DEFAULT_FLAGS control reader. Candidate exposes none.

Journal record timestamp and message construction — Reference chooses _SOURCE_REALTIME_TIMESTAMP then __REALTIME_TIMESTAMP and builds syslog-like line using host,identifier/comm,pid and message, with kernel timestamp handling. Candidate decodes MESSAGE/cursor without source timestamp.

Journal startup, resume and reopen continuity — Reference replays from max(saved journal timestamp,now-findtime), transitions to operation at startup cursor and restores matches on reopen. Candidate cursor sidecar baseline starts now and corrupt cursor reseeds.

Encoding and newline decoding — Reference validates codec, auto uses preferred encoding, decodes invalid bytes with replacement plus warning, and handles multibyte newline bytes. Candidate lacks encoding option.

Backend selection and dependency outcomes — Pinned backends are pyinotify,polling,systemd. Auto tries that sequence; explicit known backend starts at its position in the sequence and can fall through later choices on ImportError with warning. Unknown backend errors. Candidate native inotify may provide equivalent outcomes but has no explicit polling compatibility selection.

Startup vs live event-time policy — Startup ignores records older than now-findtime. Live mode replaces parsed dates if abs(int(date-now))>60; remaining dates are preserved. Candidate always processing time.

Future clamping and out-of-order failure tickets — After filter normalization future ticket time clamps to now; ticket aggregation handles arrival order via adjustTime. Candidate passes now and ring model is not yet proven equivalent.

Default date patterns and explicit pattern list — Reference has ordered/adaptive default date templates plus configured regex/strftime, EPOCH/LEPOCH/TAI64N and anchor/control tokens. Candidate supports small hardcoded ISO/BSD/epoch subset and no configurable datepattern.

Timezone and inferred year/day rollover — Reference applies explicit zone or configured fixed-offset default and infers missing year relative now with rollover. Candidate BSD parser defaults 1970 unless caller gives year.

Missing and optional timestamp context — Reference reuses recent lastDate (>now-60), optional empty match may use now, live no-date may use now; startup no-date failures are constrained by checkFindTime. Candidate has no equivalent date context.

Address/network forms and identity normalization — Reference IPv4/IPv6,CIDR,IPv4 netmask and mapped/compatible normalization determine ignore identity. Candidate CIDR parser supports numeric prefix and strict family-specific membership.

Self-address ignore control — Reference ignoreself defaults true and covers own interface/resolved names; false disables this policy. Candidate always drops unenforceable loopback/unspecified and lacks configurable general self discovery.

Per-jail ignore inheritance and empty override — Each jail has its effective inherited ignore list, local empty override and runtime add/remove semantics. Candidate per-jail CIDR arrays exist but differential behavior unverified.

File-backed ignore sets and refresh errors — Reference file: sets lazy-load with comment handling, size/mtime/inode refresh about once/second and retain old set on read failure with backoff. Candidate treats file URI as invalid CIDR.

Hostname resolution modes and one-to-many identity — usedns yes/warn resolve host to all returned IPs; warn logs resolution, no disables, raw retains matched identity. Candidate ParseResult holds one IP and no hostname mode.

Hostname ignore and DNS cache policy — Reference hostname ignore expands dynamically via cached DNS; positive/negative name/IP caches are bounded 1000 entries with 5-minute TTL in pinned implementation. Candidate ignores only literal CIDRs.

Ignore command execution and result meaning — Reference expands ticket tags then executes configured ignorecommand; successful exit0 ignores, exit1 does not, other execution failures do not imply ignore. Candidate has no command.

Ignore cache key, retention and evaluation order — Reference ignorecache key expands action/ticket tags, max-count/max-time configure cache; cached result precedes ignoreself,list,command evaluation, both positive/negative cached. Candidate has no equivalent cache.
Python regex dialect — Pinned Python re syntax/flags includes named captures, lookarounds and backreferences.
Host/address tag expansion — HOST follows usedns; ADDR/IP4/IP6 and F aliases preserve family captures.
Network subjects — SUBNET/CIDR captures preserve network identity.
Custom capture metadata — F-USER/F-PORT/F-* captures, ALT and TUPLE groups survive into action data.
Non-IP failure identity — F-ID may identify a raw object independently from captured IP.
Prefregex gating and content — Prefix gates matching, extracts F-CONTENT and merges captures with populated failregex groups taking precedence.
Ignore regex and buffer effects — Ignored matches are removed/suppressed while unmatched multiline content remains usable.
Multiline maxlines/SKIPLINES — Tuple buffers retain matched/skipped/unmatched line distinctions.
Connection correlation — MLFID merges pending fields/users; default cache is 100 entries/300 seconds.
NOFAIL/GAINED/FORGET — Control markers suppress counts, reset pending state and forget correlation with multiple-user safeguards.
Runtime filters and local overrides — Effective .conf/.local/include custom definitions load without rebuild, including modified bundled names.
Modes and backend logtype — Parameters select modes; file/journal default logtype applies only absent override.
Filter diagnostics — Expose match/miss/ignore/date/capture diagnostics and equivalent operator workflow.
Oneport/multiport/allports — Action type scopes destination ports precisely.
Protocol lists/all protocols — TCP/UDP/ICMP/all and comma lists drive independent protocol rules.
Chain/direction/interface/topology — Configured tables/families/hooks/priorities and pre-rule selectors preserve traffic topology.
Verdict and target intent — Blocktype/returntype/custom target affect observable result.
Scoped ownership — Independent jail/action scopes persist; shared realization requires equivalent scopes.
Action identity/parameters/conditionals — actname/name/init and family conditional parameters preserve separate instances.
Eager/on-demand family start — Lifecycle starts eagerly or first-ban per family.
Check/repair/restart epochs — Invariant repair/restart can invalidate epoch and reapply tickets.
Prolong/reban operations — Optional actionprolong and actionreban provide distinct calls.
Flush/stop/reload lifecycle — Distinct flush/stop/reload operations preserve per-family states.
ActionInfo/history captures — Action metadata includes identity/family/counts/times/F-*/matches/overall and jail history.
norestored side-effect suppression — Flagged actions skip restored tickets while protection can restore.
Ordered independent actions — Ordered actions continue after individual exceptions with logged outcomes.
Explicit shell action compatibility — Administrator shell actions execute after substitutions on activation only.
Dynamic substitution data semantics — Escaping and nested static/dynamic substitution preserve match data semantics.
Python ActionBase compatibility — Action module class provides jail context, lifecycle and init options.
Ticket versus realized outcomes — Reference ticket can be banned after action errors; actual outcome must be independently observable.

Failure tickets carry retry weight, actual failure count, match data, first and latest event time. Reference adjusts retry by rate estimation when the interval exceeds findtime; candidate uses a literal timestamp ring. These are different algorithms, not simply different capacity limits.
Threshold has no fixed 128-event ceiling; maxmatches limits retained text independently from failure threshold.
Manual attempt command accepts an address plus optional failure text, participates in filter policy and retains match data.

Permanent ban is a distinct -1 semantic; negative schema sentinel -2 means unknown historical duration, not permanent. Candidate unsigned duration/nullable expiry cannot express all required meanings.
Expiry comparison and rounding are operation-specific: ban admission rejects end < now, expiry removal uses now > end, database restoration excludes end <= snapshot time.
Duplicate bans can prolong existing expiry without creating another active owner; ban count, total count and action reban behavior remain distinct.
Increment policy supports formula/factor, multiplier arrays with last-element saturation, max time and random time; random addition is applied after max clamp.
Increment mode weights future retry counts for known addresses; duration escalation alone is insufficient parity. Observer avoids historical events at or before stored ban time.
Per-jail versus overall-jail history affects escalation. Overall query sums latest per-jail bancount/bantime and uses latest ban time, not count of every history row.
Retained history separates all ban events in bans from latest per-address/jail escalation row in bips; candidate has one current per-jail address state plus lifetime totals.
Retained ticket JSON includes matches and metadata used by actions; dbmaxmatches and runtime maxmatches truncate independently.
Retention purges bans by purgeage and bips by purgeage plus outdated-factor duration threshold; permanent bips are retained. Disabled jail/log cleanup waits until histories are absent.
Recidive derives repeat bans from reference ban logs, while candidate uses an internal confirmed-ban source; equivalence must include restart, restore markers and duplicate notification semantics.
Restore marks tickets as restored, avoids fresh history insertion, filters newly ignored identities, preserves original expiry subject to reference current-config correction semantics.

Natural expiry/clean service stop remove enforcement without necessarily deleting retained database history; explicit operator unban deletes history for selected jail/address. Candidate clearBan retains ban_count.

Capacity and eviction must distinguish live protection, pending actions, in-window tickets and retained escalation history. Candidate eviction may remove an unbanned address with relevant history and evict_oldest can select a banned entry.
Persistence corruption/future schema must produce explicit recovery policy, preserve diagnostic original and avoid an empty successful continuity claim. Candidate load warns and starts fresh.
Reload/restart variants preserve or clear bans according to --restart/--unban/--all/--if-exists; omitted jails are removed and changed lists/actions reconciled.
Create/start/stop jail and idle controls operate independently from daemon lifetime.
Runtime settings require complete read/write introspection including transmitter-only prefregex, logtimezone, ignorecache and bantime extras; config files alone cannot export effective runtime.
Versioned legacy CLI adapter must map invocation, text/structured output, exit status and errors; native IPC uses custom binary frames and is not legacy fail2ban socket compatibility.
Logging supports runtime level/target/syslog socket, flush/reopen and required journal/systemd semantics.

Service and CLI startup modes map config directory/socket/PID/process identity, foreground/background, startup timeout, configuration test/dump and CLI startup/operational readiness and service-manager invocation.

Importer must preserve every applicable enabled jail plus modified stock/custom assets, effective defaults and dependencies; any changed protection blocks full migration. Current importer can warn/skip then return success when any jail is enabled.
Export live runtime overrides and deliberately reconcile differences from effective on-disk configuration.

Schema-versioned snapshot export reads SQLite consistently without instantiating upstream Fail2BanDb, which opens writable, changes PRAGMAs and may upgrade/repair. Pinned reference normally uses MEMORY journal, but profile exporter must also handle WAL snapshots.

Canonical state includes active ownership/scopes, original duration/start/absolute expiry, separate retained events/latest history and source resume data; database does not encode every effective action scope without config/runtime join.

Source continuity maps file first-line fingerprint/offset and journal timestamp position, not an assumed universal journal cursor. Transient failure tickets and pending queues are not stored in source SQLite.
Inspect/plan/validate are deterministic staged operations with complete blocker classifications, source fingerprints, dependency/secret boundaries and semantic comparisons.
Cutover acquires lock, stages separately owned enforcement, reconciles final source delta, verifies active rules and quiesces previous writer at defined ingestion boundary.
Rollback incorporates post-cutover bans/unbans/expiries using ordered journal and reverse mapping, and verifies source protection before removing target effects.
Migration receipts and durable step journal distinguish success, incompatibility, validation failure, operational failure and failed rollback; replay/idempotency and clock uncertainty are explicit.

Inherited systemd socket activation — Reference honors LISTEN_PID/FDS/FDNAMES, selects named fail2ban or first inherited descriptor, consumes activation variables and marks close-on-exec. Candidate always opens new socket and unlinks path despite shipping a socket unit.

Service manager reload and firewall ordering — Reference unit orders after and PartOf firewall services, supplies ExecStop and ExecReload, and RestartPreventExitStatus. Candidate unit lacks corresponding reload and firewall lifecycle dependency contracts.

Signal-specific shutdown and log reopen — Reference handles SIGUSR1 for flushlogs and SIGTERM/SIGINT for shutdown; daemonization ignores SIGHUP. Candidate subscribes TERM/INT/HUP and logs unimplemented HUP reload, with no SIGUSR1 handler.

Shipped monitoring and completion script compatibility — Upstream monitoring/completion consumes exact client output labels, fields, jail/action lists, exit status, socket/PID and log paths. Existing generic CLI row lacks these concrete consumer fixtures.

Complete installation and upgrade asset manifest — Reference install includes configuration and local override directories, nested ignorecommands, Python actions, entrypoints, generated python binding/service templates and optional recursive test assets. Replacement packaging needs explicit equivalent inventory, ownership and dependency receipts rather than matching installer implementation.

Linux init profiles and rootless execution assumptions — Pinned tree ships multiple init families and documents running unprivileged with prearranged log/enforcement access. Applicable Linux profile must explicitly map supervisor/options/socket/PID/reload and privilege assumptions; non-Linux init files require reasoned exclusion, not hidden omission.
Alternate diagnostic configuration directory — Filter by jail/name resolves only the selected configuration base and its local/includes.
Diagnostic date override — CLI datepattern is installed first; subsequent filter datepattern cannot replace it.
Diagnostic timezone alias — --timezone and --TZ set default conversion zone.
Diagnostic input encoding — Configured codec decodes file data and formatting handles output encoding.
Diagnostic raw host mode — Raw hosts are returned for diagnostic identity rather than mandatory resolution.
Diagnostic DNS tag resolution — usedns influences tag matching and resolver policy in diagnostic filter.
Diagnostic multiline override — CLI nonzero maxlines wins over filter setting; internal display limit default differs from filter buffer.
Diagnostic journal selector override — CLI journalmatch is shlex-split and overrides filter journalmatch.
Diagnostic logger threshold — Named/numeric supported level is converted and set on diagnostic logger.
Diagnostic machine version — -V prints normalized machine-readable version and exits through callback.
Diagnostic incremental verbosity — Repeated -v/--verbose increments verbosity and controls extended reporting/errors.
Diagnostic numeric verbosity — Explicit integer verbosity controls output formatting and detailed options.
Diagnostic date details — --verbose-date/--VD expands date-pattern output.
Diagnostic generated debug links — -D/--debuggex constructs encoded debug URLs from sample and expanded regex; no external request is required.
Diagnostic regex iteration control — Disables checking all regex; output-token mode already disables check-all.
Diagnostic token/format output — Outputs chosen failure fields or formatted tokens and suppresses ordinary stats; changes pending/checkAllRegex behavior.
Diagnostic inverted output — In output-token mode selects nonmatching lines with time/message data.
Diagnostic missed-line suppression — Suppress missed-line samples while retaining summary counts.
Diagnostic ignored-line suppression — Suppress ignored-line samples while retaining ignore counts.
Diagnostic all matched lines — Include complete matched-line output with matches/counters intact.
Diagnostic all missed lines — Print missed records past default truncation threshold.
Diagnostic all ignored lines — Print all ignored records past default sample limit.
Diagnostic compact traceback logging — Adds compressed traceback context to logging formatter.
Diagnostic full traceback logging — Selects full traceback form when traceback logging is enabled.

Diagnostic positional input and filter resolution — LOG can be literal,file or systemd-journal with backend args; REGEX can be raw regex,jail/filter with brackets,or filename. Explicit IGNOREREGEX replaces loaded ignore expressions. Diagnostic checkFindTime=false must remain distinct from daemon policy.
